correctness.rationale: For positive integer x_i,y_i and two equal total-N rows, B=(1/(2N))Σ|x_i−y_i| and squared two-row CA distance X²=(2/N)Σ(x_i−y_i)²/(x_i+y_i), since column mass is (x_i+y_i)/(2N). For N=10, pairs ((1,3,6),(3,1,6)) and ((1,2,7),(2,4,4)) yield B=1/5<3/10 while X²=2/5>4/11. Independently generated every labeled positive composition for each 3≤N≤10 and each 2≤k<N, formed each unordered table pair, and independently counted strict rank inversions using sorted rational values and binary search. The exhaustive exact counts vanish N≤9 and at N=10 are 288,8256,30100,17100 for k=3,4,5,6, zero otherwise. This finite computation is an exhaustive proof because all finite admissible compositions are covered and arithmetic is exact, not a partial search.

value.rationale: Two standard ecological dissimilarities apply different abundance weightings; their first strict reversal under positive integer equal-census two-row constraints is a natural exact discretization boundary, useful for small-sample distance selection and teaching why metric rankings need not agree. The complete first richness layer, not an isolated tiny number or mere ratio calculation, is the valuable classification. No empirical abundance adequacy or broader-table extension is claimed.

scientific_limitations: Only strictly positive integer profiles with equal row totals and common labeled k; permitting zeros changes the boundary.
Column masses are computed from each two-row table itself; no transfer to pooled multitable CA column masses.
Published ecology comparisons may have unindexed finite examples.
